predecessors.name: Kakatiya dynasty
predecessors.text: Ambadeva's principality at its start: the Kadapa country of the 1287 Attirala inscription and the Tripurantakam area, where his inscriptions of 1273 and 1290 stand

successors.name: Kakatiya dynasty
successors.text: the Kadapa country and Mulikinadu, annexed in 1309 ('The region was annexed to the Kakatiya kingdom', Prataparudra II page); Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva…

ledger.x: before 1281: Ambadeva rules an independent Kayastha principality south of the Krishna.
before 1281: the principality takes the Kadapa country and the Tripurantakam area out of the Kakatiya kingdom (kakatiya-dynasty carries the matching loss).
1290: the Kakatiyas defeat Manuma Ganda-gopala and take Nellore.
1309: the Kakatiya expedition ends the Kayastha rule.
1309: Mulikinadu is annexed by the Kakatiyas: 'The region was annexed to the Kakatiya kingdom'.
1309: the Kayastha principality of Ambadeva ends: 'the end of the Kayastha rule'.

wars.name: Ambadeva's Kayastha revolt
wars.outcome: Ambadeva, chief from 1272, asserted independence, killed Rudrama in November 1289 (a theory on indirect evidence), lost Nellore (his nominee Manuma-Gandagopala) to Prataparudra in 1290 and Tripurantakam in mid-1291, and lost Mulikinadu to the Kakatiya…

certainty.note: The pages name places and inscription find-spots, not borders; the shape is two radii.
